comments.author: @empirestate8791
comments.text: The problem with low cost carriers like Spirit is that there's nothing inherently innovative that others can't copy. You have to burn the same fuel, fly the same planes, use the same airports, and hire the same pilots as other airlines. Sure you can save some money here and there (like flying older planes, using gates further away from the terminal exit, going to secondary airports, etc.), but those tradeoffs do worsen the flying experience, and it's nothing that other airlines can't do. Spirit's bare fare was innovative when it made its debut, but there was nothing preventing United and American from offering a bare fare too. And the legacy carriers have much better infrastructure and a much more diversified fleet to handle shocks like COVID and changing consumer preferences.
